title: NS Server log-derived

options.content:
Every panel here is parsed from **ns_server.stats.log** - the ns_doctor heartbeat, roughly one sample a minute - and not scraped by Prometheus. Every series is whole-node: the heartbeat reads /proc and has no cgroup view.
Prefer the scraped equivalent on **Node Overview** wherever the capture has one; panels name theirs.
These panels also cover a shorter span than the scraped stats, so they can start partway into the time range where the others do not.

_panels.title: CPU utilization / steal (heartbeat)
_panels.description:
Whole-node CPU, from sigar.

- **utilization** - percentage of the node's CPU that was busy
- **stolen** - percentage of time the hypervisor ran another guest on the vCPU (Linux VMs only)

Prefer sys_cpu_utilization_rate and the CPU attribution panels on Node Overview where the capture has them: scraped, and cgroup-aware.

_panels.title: Per-process CPU (heartbeat)
_panels.description:
CPU per process, one series for each process in the heartbeat.

Prefer sysproc_cpu_utilization on Node Overview where the capture has it: the same instrument, at scrape resolution.

_panels.title: CPU pressure - share of time stalled, avg60 (host)
_panels.description:
PSI share of time the node was stalled waiting for CPU, the kernel's 60-second average.

- **some** - share of time at least one task was stalled
- **full** - share of time every non-idle task was stalled at once; the kernel tracks this per-cgroup only, so the host series reads zero or is absent

Prefer 'CPU pressure - host vs cgroup (share of time stalled, avg10)' on Node Overview where the capture has it: scraped from 7.2.4, at avg10 and scrape resolution, host and cgroup separately. This panel is the only PSI an earlier capture has.

_panels.title: CPU pressure - stall time rate (host)
_panels.description:
Microseconds of PSI stall per second waiting for CPU, as a rate of the kernel's cumulative counter. Sampled once a minute, so a minute is the finest slice it resolves.

- **some** - time at least one task was stalled
- **full** - time every non-idle task was stalled at once; the host series reads zero or is absent, as above

Prefer 'CPU pressure - host vs cgroup (share of time stalled, avg10)' on Node Overview where the capture has it: the same counter, scraped from 7.2.4 as sys_pressure_total_stall_time_usec.

_panels.title: OS memory (memsup)
_panels.description:
The node's memory as memsup's get_system_memory_data() reports it. Which tags appear is platform-dependent, and memsup may add tags without notice.

- **total_memory** - the total amount of memory available to the Erlang emulator, allocated and free
- **system_total_memory** - the amount of memory available to the whole operating system
- **free_memory** - the amount of free memory available to the Erlang emulator for allocation
- **available_memory** - the amount of memory available for increased usage if there is an increased memory need; newer Linux kernels only, and where it is absent free + cached + buffered approximates it
- **cached_memory** - the amount of memory the system uses for cached files read from disk; on Linux, memory marked reclaimable in the kernel slab allocator is added to this too
- **buffered_memory** - the amount of memory the system uses for temporarily storing raw disk blocks
- **total_swap** - the total amount of memory the system has available for disk swap
- **free_swap** - the amount of memory the system has available for disk swap
- **shared_memory** / **largest_free** - tags memsup can return that its documentation does not describe

Prefer the sys_mem_* panels on Node Overview where the capture has them: scraped, and with the Couchbase cgroup broken out.

_panels.title: Per-process resident memory (heartbeat)
_panels.description:
Resident set size per process, one series for each process in the heartbeat. RSS includes shared pages, so the series do not sum to the node's usage.

Prefer sysproc_mem_resident on Node Overview where the capture has it: the same instrument, at scrape resolution.

_panels.title: meminfo anon/file LRU split (Linux)
_panels.description:
The kernel's reclaim lists, from /proc/meminfo. Linux only.

- **active_anon** / **inactive_anon** - anonymous pages (heaps, stacks), recently used and not; these can be swapped but not dropped
- **active_file** / **inactive_file** - file-backed page cache; the inactive half is reclaimed first
- **dirty** - pages modified and not yet written back
- **writeback** - pages being written back

_panels.title: meminfo reclaim fields (Linux)
_panels.description:
The /proc/meminfo fields describing reclaimable memory. Linux only.

- **mem_available** - the kernel's estimate of what can be allocated without swapping: free memory plus the reclaimable part of the cache
- **slab** - kernel data structures (inodes, dentries and the rest)
- **sunreclaim** - the part of slab that cannot be reclaimed
- **percpu** - per-CPU allocator memory

_panels.title: Erlang memory breakdown (erlang:memory)
_panels.description:
Memory dynamically allocated by the Erlang emulator, from erlang:memory(). More types may be added in a future release.

- **total** - the total amount of memory currently allocated; the same as the sum of processes and system
- **processes** - the total amount of memory currently allocated for the Erlang processes
- **processes_used** - the amount of that currently used by the Erlang processes
- **system** - memory currently allocated for the emulator that is not directly related to any Erlang process
- **atom** - memory currently allocated for atoms; part of system
- **atom_used** - the amount of that currently used
- **binary** - memory currently allocated for binaries; part of system
- **code** - memory currently allocated for Erlang code; part of system
- **ets** - memory currently allocated for ETS tables; part of system

The series overlap rather than partition the total, so they do not add up: system = atom + binary + code + ets + other system memory, and processes = processes_used + the rest.

The docs note this accounting is approximate: system is incomplete, that error carries into total, and the amounts are not gathered atomically. total is not meant to equal the emulator's mapped pages - it excludes shared libraries, the emulator's own code and its stacks, while fragmentation and prereservation mean the segments holding it can be much larger.

_panels.title: Worst Erlang process memory (memsup)
_panels.description:
The largest single Erlang process on the node by allocated bytes, as memsup's get_memory_data() reports it, labelled with its pid and, where diag.log's process dump names it, its registered name or initial call.

The largest process is re-picked at every sample, so a series starts and stops as the winner changes.

memsup returns the result of its latest memory check rather than running a fresh one, so a sample can lag its timestamp by up to the check interval - one minute by default. The value is undefined where memsup is configured not to collect process data (memsup_system_only).

_panels.title: Memory pressure - share of time stalled, avg60 (host)
_panels.description:
PSI share of time the node was stalled waiting on memory reclaim, the kernel's 60-second average.

- **some** - share of time at least one task was stalled
- **full** - share of time every non-idle task was stalled at once

Prefer 'Memory pressure - host vs cgroup (share of time stalled, avg10)' on Node Overview where the capture has it: scraped from 7.2.4, at avg10 and scrape resolution, host and cgroup separately. This panel is the only PSI an earlier capture has.

_panels.title: Memory pressure - stall time rate (host)
_panels.description:
Microseconds of PSI stall per second waiting on memory reclaim, as a rate of the kernel's cumulative counter. Sampled once a minute, so a minute is the finest slice it resolves.

- **some** - time at least one task was stalled
- **full** - time every non-idle task was stalled at once

Prefer 'Memory pressure - host vs cgroup (share of time stalled, avg10)' on Node Overview where the capture has it: the same counter, scraped from 7.2.4 as sys_pressure_total_stall_time_usec.

_panels.title: Memory allocation stalls (10m increase)
_panels.description: Direct-reclaim stalls per 10-minute window, from the kernel's allocstall counter: the kernel counts one each time an allocation could not be met from free memory and the allocating task reclaimed memory itself rather than leaving it to kswapd. Linux only.

_panels.title: IO pressure - share of time stalled, avg60 (host)
_panels.description:
PSI share of time the node was stalled waiting on IO, the kernel's 60-second average.

- **some** - share of time at least one task was stalled
- **full** - share of time every non-idle task was stalled at once

Prefer 'IO pressure - host vs cgroup (share of time stalled, avg10)' on Node Overview where the capture has it: scraped from 7.2.4, at avg10 and scrape resolution, host and cgroup separately. This panel is the only PSI an earlier capture has.

_panels.title: IO pressure - stall time rate (host)
_panels.description:
Microseconds of PSI stall per second waiting on IO, as a rate of the kernel's cumulative counter. Sampled once a minute, so a minute is the finest slice it resolves.

- **some** - time at least one task was stalled
- **full** - time every non-idle task was stalled at once

Prefer 'IO pressure - host vs cgroup (share of time stalled, avg10)' on Node Overview where the capture has it: the same counter, scraped from 7.2.4 as sys_pressure_total_stall_time_usec.

_panels.title: Disk usage by mount (disksup)
_panels.description: Percentage full per mount, as Erlang's disksup reports it: every mount it checks, tmpfs included. disksup runs on its own timer rather than per heartbeat, so the series step rather than curve. Mount sizes are backfilled too, as heartbeat_disk_capacity_bytes.

description:
Metrics parsed out of ns_server logs, not scraped from Prometheus: every panel comes from the ns_doctor heartbeat in ns_server.stats.log, roughly one sample a minute, mixing OS instruments (meminfo, PSI, sigar) with Erlang-VM instruments (erlang:memory, memsup). Collection gaps are drawn as breaks in the line.

Prefer the scraped stats wherever the capture has them: Node Overview carries most of these instruments at scrape resolution and separates the host from the Couchbase cgroup. The heartbeat reads /proc and has no cgroup view, so every series here is whole-node. Panels name their Node Overview equivalent where there is one.

The heartbeat also covers a shorter span than the scraped stats, bounded by size rather than time: stats.log keeps 40 MiB per file over 10 rotations, all of which cbcollect concatenates, and each dump covers every node and bucket, so the span narrows as a cluster grows - a couple of days is typical, less on a large one. These panels can therefore start partway into the time range where the others do not.
